lessons.title: Explore Integers and Their Opposites
lessons.objective: I can use integers to represent quantities in everyday life, explain what 0 means in each situation, and name the opposite of an integer on the number line.
lessons.languageObjective: I can explain my reasoning using the words integer, opposite, negative, positive, and number line.

concept.heading: How do you use integers to describe quantities above and below zero?
concept.intro: Counting numbers, their opposites, and 0 are integers. A negative integer is less than zero and is written with a − sign. Opposites are the same distance from 0, but on opposite sides of the number line.
concept.keyIdea: Integers & Opposites. 1. Integers: Positive whole numbers, negative whole numbers, and zero (..., -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, ...). 2. Opposites: Numbers that are the same distance from 0 in opposite directions (e.g. -5 and 5). 3. The opposite of the opposite of a number is the number itself: -(-a) = a

worked.title: Watch me
lines: Badwater Basin is 86 meters below sea level, and sea level is defined as 0.
Below 0 means a negative number, so I write the elevation as −86 meters.
On a number line, I count 86 units to the LEFT of 0 and mark that point.
The opposite of −86 is 86. Both are 86 units from 0, just on different sides.
linesEs: La cuenca de Badwater está 86 metros bajo el nivel del mar, y el nivel del mar se define como 0.
Debajo de 0 significa un número negativo, así que escribo la elevación como −86 metros.
En una recta numérica, cuento 86 unidades a la izquierda del 0 y marco ese punto.
El opuesto de −86 es 86. Los dos están a 86 unidades del 0, solo que en lados distintos.

together.title: Let's try together
lines: One day in January the temperature in Toronto was 9°C and in Reykjavik it was −9°C.
Which one is to the left of 0 on the number line? The negative sign tells us: −9.
How many units from 0 is 9? How many units from 0 is −9? Both are 9 units.
So 9 and −9 are opposites — same distance from 0, opposite sides.
linesEs: Un día de enero la temperatura en Toronto fue de 9 °C y en Reikiavik fue de −9 °C.
¿Cuál está a la izquierda del 0 en la recta numérica? El signo negativo nos lo dice: −9.
¿A cuántas unidades del 0 está el 9? ¿A cuántas unidades del 0 está el −9? Los dos están a 9 unidades.
Entonces 9 y −9 son opuestos — a la misma distancia del 0, en lados opuestos.

vocabulary.definition: The counting numbers, their opposites, and 0.
A number that is the same distance from 0 as another number, but on the other side of 0.
vocabulary.example: 86 and -86 are both 86 units from 0, on opposite sides

vocabulary.definition: A number less than 0, written with a − sign. On a number line it sits to the left of 0.
vocabulary.example: -86 meters means 86 meters BELOW sea level

vocabulary.definition: A number greater than 0. On a number line it sits to the right of 0.
vocabulary.example: 9°C is 9 degrees ABOVE zero

vocabulary.definition: A straight line where numbers are placed in order. It extends to the left of 0 to show values less than 0.
vocabulary.example: -3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3 marked in order from left to right

vocabulary.definition: Taking the opposite twice brings you back to the first number.

lessons.title: Represent Rational Numbers and Their Opposites on the Number Line
lessons.objective: I can place rational numbers, including fractions and decimals, on a number line.
lessons.languageObjective: I can explain my reasoning using the words rational number, fraction, decimal, and number line.

concept.heading: How do you place rational numbers on a number line?
concept.intro: A rational number can be written as a ratio of two integers with a nonzero denominator. Integers and terminating or repeating decimals are rational. A rational number that is not an integer lies between two neighboring integers.
concept.keyIdea: Rational Numbers on the Number Line. 1. Find the two consecutive integers the rational number falls between. 2. Divide the segment between integers into equal parts matching the denominator. 3. Negative numbers move to the left of zero; positive numbers move to the right

worked.title: Watch me
lines: I will plot -2.5 on the number line.
First, the integers it falls between: -2.5 is between -2 and -3.
The .5 means halfway, so I split the space between -2 and -3 in half.
I place my dot exactly halfway between -2 and -3. That is -2.5.
linesEs: Voy a marcar -2.5 en la recta numérica.
Primero, los números enteros entre los que cae: -2.5 está entre -2 y -3.
El .5 significa a la mitad, así que parto en dos el espacio entre -2 y -3.
Coloco mi punto exactamente a la mitad entre -2 y -3. Ese es -2.5.

together.title: Let's try together
lines: Now let's plot 0.75. Which two integers is it between? It is between 0 and 1.
The decimal 0.75 equals the fraction 3/4. The denominator 4 splits one unit into four equal parts; the numerator 3 counts three parts.
So we split 0 to 1 into 4 equal parts and place the dot at the 3rd mark.
linesEs: Ahora marquemos 0.75. ¿Entre qué dos números enteros está? Está entre 0 y 1.
El decimal 0.75 equivale a la fracción 3/4. El denominador 4 divide una unidad en cuatro partes iguales; el numerador 3 cuenta tres partes.
Así que partimos de 0 a 1 en 4 partes iguales y colocamos el punto en la 3.ª marca.

vocabulary.term: Rational Numbers on the Number Line
vocabulary.definition: Every rational number has one exact spot on the number line. Writing it as a fraction, a decimal, or an integer does not change where it sits.
vocabulary.example: −3/2 = −1.5 and 1/2 = 0.5 each sit at one exact point.

vocabulary.definition: A number that can be written as a fraction of two integers, with a bottom number that is not zero.
vocabulary.example: −1/2, 0 and 5/4 each sit at one exact point.

vocabulary.definition: A number that shows part of a whole, like 3/4.
vocabulary.example: 3/4 means 3 out of 4 equal parts — like 3 slices of a pizza cut into 4

vocabulary.definition: A number with a dot, like 0.5, that shows a part less than one.
vocabulary.example: 0.5 = 1/2 (halfway between 0 and 1 on the number line)

vocabulary.definition: A straight line where numbers are placed in order; numbers get smaller to the left and larger to the right.
Having the same value, just written a different way.
vocabulary.example: 1/2 = 0.5 = 2/4 — all name the same point on the number line

vocabulary.definition: Whole numbers and their opposites, like -2, -1, 0, 1, 2.
A number the same distance from 0 on the other side of 0.

support.prompt: In Reykjavik the temperature was -9°C. What is the opposite of -9?
support.explanation: The opposite of a number is the same distance from 0 on the other side, so the opposite of -9 is 9.
feedback: Doubling the distance from 0 is not the same as crossing to the other side. The opposite keeps the distance 9 and only changes the direction.
A number cannot be its own opposite unless it is 0. The opposite of a negative number is on the other side of 0, so it is positive.
Zero is its own opposite, but it is not the opposite of -9 — it is 9 units away from -9, not on the far side of 0.
hints: 'Opposite' means the same distance from 0, but on the other side of 0.
-9 sits 9 units to the LEFT of 0. Count 9 units to the RIGHT of 0 instead.
Keep the 9 exactly the same and change only the direction, which means changing only the sign.

choices: A number written -0, which is less than 0
support.explanation: Zero is 0 units from itself, so there is no other side to move to. Zero is its own opposite.
feedback: There is no separate point for -0 on the number line. Writing a negative sign in front of 0 still names the same single point, 0.
The opposite of a number is one specific number, not a whole group of them. Every number has exactly one opposite.
Zero does have an opposite. Since its distance from 0 is 0, it lands right back on itself.
hints: The opposite of a number is the same distance from 0 on the other side.
Ask yourself: how many units away from 0 is 0 itself?
If a number is 0 units from 0, moving to the other side takes you to the very same point.

support.prompt: Spot the Mistake: The Opposite of -7
steps: Student thinking: The number starts out negative, and taking the opposite of a negative number keeps it negative, so the answer stays on the left side of 0.
Student answer: The opposite of -7 is -7.
support.explanation: Opposites are the same distance from 0 but on OPPOSITE sides of 0. -7 sits 7 units to the left of 0, so its opposite must sit 7 units to the RIGHT of 0. That number is 7. The only integer that is its own opposite is 0, because 0 is zero units from itself.
hints: What does the word 'opposite' require about which side of 0 a number is on?
Count how many units -7 is from 0, then count that same distance in the other direction.
Mark -7 on a number line, count the 7 units back to 0, then keep counting 7 more units in the same direction past 0.

support.prompt: Which point is located between -1 and -2 on the number line?
support.explanation: -1.5 is between -1 and -2 because it is 0.5 units to the left of -1 (or 0.5 units to the right of -2).
feedback: This value is farther left than -2, so it lands between -2 and -3. Look for a number just past -1 heading toward -2.
-0.5 sits between 0 and -1 — it has not traveled past -1 yet. You need a number that lands beyond -1 but before -2.
That value is positive, which puts it on the right side of 0. Both -1 and -2 sit to the left of 0, so the number you need is negative.
hints: 'Between -1 and -2' is on the NEGATIVE side, in the gap from -1 to -2.
Turn each choice into a spot on the number line and check: is it past -1 but not past -2?
Start at -1 and move half a unit farther left. Which choice lands in that gap between -1 and -2?

feedback: Not quite. 0.25 means 25 hundredths = 25/100 = ___.
This fraction is about 0.333, so it is bigger than 0.25. Convert the decimal into hundredths and reduce that fraction.
This fraction equals 0.4 as a decimal, which is larger than 0.25. Write 0.25 as a fraction over 100 first, then simplify.
hints: Read 0.25 as a place-value number: 25 hundredths.
Write it as 25/100, then simplify by dividing the top and bottom by the same number.
Divide both 25 and 100 by 25. What simpler fraction do you get?

support.prompt: Where is -3/4 located on the number line?
support.explanation: -3/4 = -0.75, which is between 0 and -1. It is 3/4 of the way from 0 toward -1.
feedback: Not quite. -3/4 = -0.75, which is between ___ and ___.
-3/4 is less than one whole unit away from 0, so it never even reaches -1. Convert the fraction to a decimal and see how far left it travels.
The distance is right, but the negative sign puts this number to the left of 0, not to the right.
hints: The size of -3/4 is less than 1 whole — its distance from zero is under 1.
Convert: 3/4 = 0.75, so -3/4 = -0.75. Now ask which two numbers -0.75 sits between on the line.
Start at 0 and move 0.75 units LEFT. Did you pass -1 on the way, or not?

steps: Problem: Plot 1.5 on the number line.
Student thinking: 1.5 has a 1 and a 5, so I will plot it between 1 and 5.
Student answer: Point plotted at about 3, halfway between 1 and 5.
support.explanation: 1.5 does NOT mean between 1 and 5. The .5 is one half, so 1.5 is halfway between 1 and 2. I find the two neighboring integers it falls between (1 and 2), split that space in half, and place the dot at the middle. The point belongs at 1.5, not 3.
hints: What does the .5 in 1.5 mean — is it a separate whole number or a part of one?
Which two integers is 1.5 between? Split that space into equal parts.

support.prompt: Predict the distance of first point from zero for these settings. Give the answer in units. Round to four decimal places if needed.
support.explanation: |-4| = 4; opposite = 4. -4 < 6. Absolute values: 4 and 6. Farther right means greater.
hints: Identify which quantities the requested measure uses.
Use the relationship you explored in Investigate. Check with a second method.

support.explanation: Opposites lie on different sides of zero at equal distances. The opposite is 2.5.
hints: Name the given quantities and the quantity you need.
Draw a model or write the relationship first. Check your answer in the original situation.

support.explanation: Absolute value measures distance from zero: |−4| = 4 units.
hints: Name the given quantities and the quantity you need.
Draw a model or write the relationship first. Check your answer in the original situation.

core.prompt: Which list of integers is ordered from LEAST to GREATEST?
core.explanation: Least to greatest reads left to right on the number line: -8, then -3, then 0, then 5.
feedback: The two negatives are swapped. Among negative integers, the one with the larger digit is farther LEFT of 0, which makes it the smaller value.
Zero is not the least value here. Every negative integer sits to the left of 0, so both negatives must come before it.
This list runs greatest to least. The question asks for the smallest value first.
hints: Least to greatest means left to right on a number line.
Split the list into negatives and positives first — every negative integer is less than 0 and less than every positive integer.
Between -8 and -3, which one is farther to the left of 0? That number starts the list.

choices: 0 is an integer, and it is its own opposite
0 is a negative integer because it is not positive
0 is a positive integer because it has no negative sign
0 is not an integer at all
core.explanation: Integers are the counting numbers, their opposites, and 0. Zero is 0 units from itself, so it is its own opposite.
feedback: Negative integers are less than 0, and 0 is not less than itself. Zero is neither negative nor positive.
Positive integers are greater than 0, and 0 is not greater than itself. The missing sign does not make it positive.
Zero is explicitly part of the definition: integers are the counting numbers, their opposites, and 0.
hints: Reread the definition of integer — check whether 0 is named in it.
Positive means greater than 0 and negative means less than 0. Is 0 either one?
For the opposite, ask how many units 0 is from itself, then move that distance to the other side.

core.prompt: Spot the Mistake: Reykjavik's Temperature Swing
steps: Problem: At 6 a.m. in Reykjavik the temperature was -12°C. At 2 p.m. it was the opposite of the 6 a.m. temperature. What was the temperature at 2 p.m.?
Student thinking: The opposite of a temperature should still be a cold temperature, so I keep the negative sign and just make the number bigger. That gives a temperature farther from 0.
Student answer: The temperature at 2 p.m. was -24°C.
core.explanation: An opposite never changes the distance from 0 — it changes only the side. -12 is 12 units to the left of 0, so its opposite is 12 units to the RIGHT of 0, which is 12°C. The 2 p.m. temperature was 12°C. (If you then take the opposite again for 11 p.m., you come back to -12°C.)
hints: Does taking an opposite change how far a number is from 0, or only which side it is on?
Count the units: -12 is 12 units from 0. Where is the point that is also 12 units from 0?
Mark -12 and count the 12 units up to 0. Continue that same 12 units above 0 and read the temperature you land on.

core.prompt: Which rational number is closest to 0 on the number line?
core.explanation: |-1/4| = 0.25, |0.5| = 0.5, |-2| = 2, |1.75| = 1.75. Since 0.25 is the smallest absolute value, -1/4 is closest to zero.
feedback: Distance from 0 is what matters here, and this number sits a full 2 units away. Compare absolute values rather than signs.
|0.5| = 0.5, but one negative option sits even closer to zero than that. Distance ignores sign — compare absolute values before ruling out the negatives.
This value is almost 2 units from 0. Convert every option to a decimal and compare how far each one is from zero, ignoring direction.
hints: 'Closest to 0' means the SMALLEST distance from zero — the sign doesn't matter.
Find each choice's absolute value — for example |0.5| = 0.5 — then look for the smallest distance.
Write every choice as a distance from zero, then compare all four distances and take the smallest.

core.prompt: Which number is farthest to the LEFT on a number line?
core.explanation: Farther left means more negative: -4 < -1 < 0 < 2, so -4 is farthest left.
feedback: Not quite. Farther left means more negative: ___ < -1 < 0 < 2, so ___ is farthest left.
Zero is the dividing point, not the far left end. Every negative number sits to the left of it.
Positive numbers sit to the right of 0, so this is the wrong direction. Farther left means more negative.
hints: Farthest LEFT means the least value — the most negative number.
Sketch the line: negatives sit left of 0, and among negatives, a bigger distance from zero is farther left.
Place -1 and -4 on the line: count how far below zero each one sits. Which is farther out?

core.explanation: The opposite of a number is its reflection across 0, so the opposite of -3/4 is 3/4.
feedback: -3/4 is the number itself, unchanged. An opposite reflects across 0 — same distance, other side — so the sign has to switch.
Zero is its own opposite and sits at the center. The opposite of a number is the same distance from 0, just on the other side.
Flipping the numerator and denominator gives a reciprocal, not an opposite. An opposite keeps the same distance from 0 and changes only the direction.
hints: 'Opposite' means the mirror image across zero — same distance, other side.
Keep the size 3/4 the same and flip the sign. (Don't flip the fraction upside down — that's a reciprocal.)
-3/4 sits 3/4 of a unit LEFT of zero. Mark the point the same distance on the RIGHT — that's its opposite.

steps: Problem: Plot -2.25 on the number line.
Student thinking: It is negative, so I go past -2. The .25 is one quarter, so I count toward 0 (to the right) by a quarter unit and land between -2 and -1.
Student answer: Point plotted at -1.75, between -2 and -1.
core.explanation: Going more negative means moving LEFT, not right. -2.25 is between -2 and -3 (it is a quarter of a unit to the LEFT of -2), not between -2 and -1. I split the space from -2 to -3 into 4 equal parts and place the dot at the first mark past -2, at -2.25.
hints: On a number line, which direction is 'more negative' — left or right?
Which two integers is -2.25 between? It is just past -2 heading toward -3.

core.explanation: |-3.5| = 3.5; opposite = 3.5. -3.5 < 6. Absolute values: 3.5 and 6. Farther right means greater.
hints: Identify which quantities the requested measure uses.

stretch.prompt: At 6 a.m. in Reykjavik the temperature was -12°C. At 2 p.m. it was the opposite of the 6 a.m. temperature, and at 11 p.m. it was the opposite of the 2 p.m. temperature. What were the temperatures at 2 p.m. and 11 p.m.?
stretch.explanation: The opposite of -12 is 12, so 2 p.m. was 12°C. The opposite of 12 is -12, so 11 p.m. was back to -12°C.
feedback: The two times are switched. The first opposite is taken from -12, so 2 p.m. has to land on the positive side of 0.
Zero is its own opposite, so the opposite of -12 cannot be 0. An opposite stays the same distance from 0, which is 12 units here.
The 2 p.m. reading is right, but the second step doubled the distance from 0 instead of crossing back over 0. The opposite of 12 keeps the distance 12.
hints: Take the opposites one step at a time — start with the 6 a.m. reading.
An opposite keeps the same distance from 0 and changes only the side, so -12 becomes a positive number that is still 12 units from 0.
Now take the opposite of your 2 p.m. answer. What happens when you take the opposite of an opposite?

stretch.prompt: A football team starts at the line of scrimmage, which is 0. During one series they had a 10-yard loss, a 4-yard gain, a 3-yard loss, and a 21-yard gain. Where does the series leave them?
choices: 8 yards past the line of scrimmage
12 yards past the line of scrimmage
18 yards past the line of scrimmage
38 yards past the line of scrimmage
stretch.explanation: Write each play as an integer: -10, 4, -3, 21. Combining them gives -10 + 4 - 3 + 21 = 12, so the team ends 12 yards past the line of scrimmage.
feedback: The 4-yard gain got left out of the count. Every play changes the team's position, gains and losses alike.
The 3-yard loss was counted as a gain here. A loss moves the team backward, so it is a negative integer.
This adds all four plays as if every one were a gain. Losses have to be written as negative integers before you combine them.
hints: The line of scrimmage is 0. Which plays move the team below 0, and which move it above?
Write all four plays as integers first: gains are positive and losses are negative.
Combine -10, 4, -3, and 21 in order, keeping every sign. Where do you land compared to 0?

stretch.prompt: Describe two different real-world situations that use negative integers. For each one, tell exactly what 0 means in that situation, write one negative integer it could produce, and explain what the opposite of that integer would mean in the same situation.
stretch.frame: My first situation is ___. In it, 0 means ___, so ___ would represent ___. The opposite of that integer is ___, which would mean ___.
stretch.explanation: Every situation that uses negative integers has a chosen zero. With elevation, 0 is sea level, so -30 meters means 30 meters below the surface and its opposite, 30, means 30 meters above it. With temperature, 0 is zero degrees, so -5°C is five degrees below zero and its opposite, 5°C, is five degrees above. In both cases the opposite is the same distance from 0, just measured in the other direction, which is what makes it the mirror image of the original quantity.
hints: Think about places where a measurement can go both above and below a starting point: elevation, temperature, money, football yardage.
Name the starting point out loud — that is your 0. Then a quantity below it is your negative integer.
For the opposite, keep the same distance from 0 and cross to the other side, then say what that new number means in your story.

stretch.prompt: On a number line, point P is located at -2.5. Which statement describes its location best?
feedback: -2.5 has not traveled all the way to -3. The .5 means it stops partway between two integers.
Not quite. -2.5 sits exactly halfway between ___ and ___.
The distance is right, but the sign got dropped. A negative value sits on the left side of 0.
hints: The .5 in -2.5 means half a unit MORE negative than -2.
Start at -2 on the number line and move another half unit left. Describe where you land relative to -2 and -3.
Mark -2 and -3, then place -2.5. Is it nearer to -2, nearer to -3, or exactly in the middle of them?

stretch.prompt: Which list of numbers is ordered from LEAST to GREATEST?
stretch.explanation: Least to greatest runs most-negative to most-positive: -5, -2, 0, 3.
feedback: The two negatives are out of order here. Among negative numbers, the one with the larger digit sits farther left, which makes it the smaller value.
This list jumps back and forth across 0. Least to greatest has to move steadily left to right along the number line.
Not quite. Least to greatest runs most-negative to most-positive: ___.
hints: Least to greatest starts at the MOST negative number and climbs toward the positives.
Check each list: negatives must come first (farthest below zero leading), then 0, then the positives.
Compare -5 and -2 on a number line: which is farther below zero? The correct list starts with that number.

steps: Problem: Plot -3/4 on the number line
Student thinking: -3/4 has a 3 and a 4, so I go to -3 on the number line and then count 4 more to the left
stretch.explanation: -3/4 means negative three-fourths, which is 3/4 of the way from 0 toward -1. It should be plotted between 0 and -1, not at -7. The student treated the numerator and denominator as separate integers.
hints: What does the fraction 3/4 actually mean? How much of a whole is it?
-3/4 is a number between 0 and -1. It is 3/4 of one unit to the left of zero.

stretch.prompt: Name three different rational numbers between -1 and 0. Write each as both a fraction and a decimal. Explain how you know they are between -1 and 0.
stretch.frame: Three rational numbers between -1 and 0 are: ___ = ___, ___ = ___, and ___ = ___. I know they are between -1 and 0 because ___.
stretch.explanation: Any negative number greater than −1 works, so pick friendly fractions and convert them: −1/2 = −0.5, −1/4 = −0.25, and −3/10 = −0.3. Each is negative, so it sits left of 0, but each has an absolute value less than 1, so it never reaches −1. On the number line all three land inside the single unit between −1 and 0.
hints: You need numbers that are negative but greater than -1 — think of small negative fractions.
Pick easy fractions like halves, fourths, or tenths, make them negative, and write each one's decimal twin.
Test -1/2: as a decimal it's -0.5, which is left of 0 but right of -1 — so it works. Find two more like it.

hints: Identify which quantities the requested measure uses.
